package.name: xai-grok
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# XAI GROK, fully declarative.
#
# The node is a REALTIME VOICE session, not a text agent — `wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime` — so what
# unblocked it was `transport: ws` and the audio lane, built for openai-realtime. Its protocol is
# identical to OpenAI's realtime format event for event, which is why shared/tools.yaml reads the same.
#
# TWO SOCKETS ARE INVOLVED and only one is here: the vendor socket is this manifest's `run`, while the
# platform's audio socket to the browser is api/audio.yaml. That second lane exists only because MCP
# cannot carry binary audio; everything else this node emits reaches the client over MCP streaming.

name: xai-grok
displayName: xAI Grok
description: Voice conversations, image generation and video generation with xAI's Grok
# 2.1.0: grok-voice-think-fast-2.0 (model picker + reasoning dial + gated transcription), plus the
# transcript-accumulation and Q/A-log fixes proven live on the sibling realtime voice node.
# 2.2.0: Grok Imagine joins the package — XAIGrokImage (imagine-image-2.0, synchronous) and
# XAIGrokVideo (imagine-video-1.5, an async job the poll capability waits on).
# 2.3.0: XAIGrokVideoExtend — chained shots via /v1/videos/extensions, because one 15-second
# generation compresses a construction-to-function arc too far (probed live 2026-08-15).
version: 2.3.0
category: ai
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1777865512/gravity/icons/X_logo.jpg

features:
  - Realtime voice conversation with Grok, with MCP tool calling
  - Image generation with Grok Imagine, typography-strong, hosted URLs back
  - Short video generation from a prompt or a still image, with sound
  - Video extension, continuing an existing clip shot by shot

allowedHosts:
  - api.x.ai

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [bearer]
  # ws carries the voice session; json carries the Imagine REST calls.
  transport: [ws, json]
  # The video node waits on a render job. Without `poll` it would settle on the job RECEIPT
  # and emit that as the answer, with nothing anywhere reporting a problem.
  poll: true

credentials.xaiCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: xaiCredential
displayName: xAI
description: Credentials for xAI Grok API
documentationUrl: https://console.x.ai

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your xAI API key
    placeholder: xai-

shared.tools.yaml:
# The xAI Grok REALTIME tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does not belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it does not
# belong copied into a node either. It belongs here, exactly as `openai/shared/tools.yaml` holds the
# Responses protocol — imported whole:
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#
# WHY THIS IS NOT `openai/shared/tools.yaml`. Same vendor, different API, and three real differences
# rather than cosmetic ones:
#
#   the call event   Responses says `response.output_item.done` and needs a `when` to tell a function
#                    call from any other completed item. Realtime has a dedicated
#                    `response.function_call_arguments.done`, so no `when` is needed.
#   no toolsInto     Responses puts the tool list in each REQUEST. A realtime session declares it
#                    ONCE in the handshake, so there is no request field to name; run.yaml reads
#                    `services.mcpService.tools` into session.update itself.
#   no continuity    Responses chains turns with previous_response_id. THE SOCKET IS THE CONTINUITY:
#                    the conversation never ended, so there is nothing to chain.
#
# Also absent, and deliberately: `maxTurns` and `stuckAfterRepeats`. Both count turns, and a turn is
# one model call. Nothing to count here. What bounds a runaway session is the executor's own idle and
# duration ceiling.

# How ONE tool is offered. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters }

# HOW THE LIST IS RE-OFFERED once it has grown mid-call. A socket sends its tools once at the
# handshake, so growth has to be announced on purpose — this message is that announcement.
#
# ONLY `tools` in the session block: session.update MERGES rather than replaces (verified live on
# OpenAI 2026-08-12; xAI documents the same session.update semantics), so instructions, voice and
# turn detection survive untouched. Re-sending the whole session would be a second copy of the
# handshake, free to drift. No `type: realtime` key — xAI's session object does not carry one.
offer: >-
  return { type: 'session.update', session: { tools: tools } }

# How a call ARRIVES. `match` is what makes a stream tractable: events keep coming for the whole
# conversation, and this says which of them is a tool call rather than a transcript or audio.
call:
  match: response.function_call_arguments.done
  id: "return response.call_id"
  name: "return response.name"
  # A JSON STRING, which the executor parses. The trap the schema warns about: passed through
  # unparsed, the tool receives a string where it expected its parameters.
  arguments: "return response.arguments"

# How the result goes BACK. TWO messages, because OpenAI separates them: the output joins the
# conversation, then a response is asked for. Without the second the model holds the result silently.
result: >-
  return [
    { type: 'conversation.item.create',
      item: { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output } },
    { type: 'response.create' }
  ]

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# `calls.generate` is the FINAL poll payload (status done), not the start receipt — the poll
# capability's contract.

- emit: videoUrl
  from: response
  value: "return ((calls.generate || {}).video || {}).url || ''"

- emit: video
  from: response
  value: >-
    return {
      url: ((calls.generate || {}).video || {}).url || '',
      duration: ((calls.generate || {}).video || {}).duration || 0,
      respectModeration: ((calls.generate || {}).video || {}).respect_moderation === true
    }

# `generatedAt` is epoch milliseconds: the sandbox exposes Date.now() and refuses `new`.
- emit: metadata
  from: response
  value: >-
    return {
      model: (calls.generate || {}).model || 'grok-imagine-video-1.5',
      generatedAt: Date.now()
    }
files.api/run.yaml:
# One JOB: start the render, poll until done. THE MODEL IS FIXED at grok-imagine-video-1.5,
# the current GA id (docs.x.ai REST reference, 2026-08-15); the bare `grok-imagine-video`
# alias is deliberately not used, so a silent vendor re-route cannot change output under a
# saved workflow. When a second id ships this becomes a config enum, as the voice node's did.

- name: generate
  method: POST
  url: https://api.x.ai/v1/videos/generations
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.xaiCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 120000
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

  body:
    model: grok-imagine-video-1.5
    # Optional with a starting image, required without one — the vendor enforces the second
    # half, so an empty prompt on a text-only run fails at the API with its own message
    # rather than being second-guessed here. `undefined` drops the key when serialised.
    prompt: "return String(config.prompt || '').trim() || undefined"
    # The still to animate. The vendor takes { url } with a public URL or a base64 data URL.
    image: >-
      return String(config.imageUrl || '').trim()
        ? { url: String(config.imageUrl).trim() }
        : undefined
    duration: "return config.duration || 8"
    aspect_ratio: "return config.aspectRatio || '16:9'"
    resolution: "return config.resolution || '720p'"

  # THE REPLY IS THE FINAL STATUS PAYLOAD, not the start receipt: the POST answers only
  # { request_id }, and polling GET /v1/videos/{id} until `done` is what produces the video.
  #
  # `until` is asked of the start reply first (a receipt has no status, so it polls), and
  # `failed` is written because without it a terminally failed render is polled to the
  # attempt ceiling and reports a timeout instead of the reason.
  #
  # 5s x 240 = twenty minutes. A 720p render takes ~25 seconds, but 1080p at 15 seconds is
  # the honest worst case and a bound set for the fast job fails exactly the slow one.
  poll:
    url: "return 'https://api.x.ai/v1/videos/' + response.request_id"
    until: "return response.status === 'done'"
    failed: "return response.status === 'failed'"
    message: "return 'Video generation failed. ' + JSON.stringify(response.error || response)"
    intervalMs: 5000
    maxAttempts: 240
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    prompt:
      type: string
      title: Motion Prompt
      description: >-
        What happens in the video — the motion, camera and mood. Required when generating
        from text alone; with a starting image it may be left empty and the model animates
        the scene as it sees it.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:ai":
        editable: true
    imageUrl:
      type: string
      title: Starting Image URL
      description: >-
        A still to animate — the video opens on this exact frame. Wire in an image made
        upstream (e.g. images.0.url from an image step) or paste any public image URL.
        Leave empty to generate from the prompt alone.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    duration:
      type: number
      title: Duration (seconds)
      description: How long the video runs. Longer costs proportionally more.
      default: 8
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 15
    aspectRatio:
      type: string
      title: Aspect Ratio
      description: The shape of the frame.
      enum: ["16:9", "9:16", "1:1", "4:3", "3:4", "3:2", "2:3"]
      default: "16:9"
    resolution:
      type: string
      title: Resolution
      description: 1080p renders sharpest and slowest; 480p is the fast draft.
      enum: [480p, 720p, 1080p]
      default: 720p
"ui:order": [prompt, imageUrl, duration, aspectRatio, resolution]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes, referenceable in the prompt and image url
    required: false

outputs:
  # The plain string first: a template shows a video by its URL, and reaching into an object
  # for the one field everyone wants is friction with no information in it.
  - name: videoUrl
    type: string
    description: The finished video, as a hosted URL
  - name: video
    type: object
    description: "The full result: url, duration (seconds), respectModeration"
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: model, generatedAt

credentials:
  - name: xaiCredential
    required: true
    displayName: xAI
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: XAIGrokVideo
# PromiseNode WITH `poll`: generation is an async job (POST returns a request_id, GET reports
# progress), but the node's answer is still one settled reply — the finished video. Only the
# LAST call's transport decides kind, and poll changes nothing there.
kind: PromiseNode

name: Grok Video
category: Media & Design
color: "#000000"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1777865512/gravity/icons/X_logo.jpg

description: Generate short videos from a prompt or a still image with Grok Imagine

whenToUse: >-
  Turn a description or a still image into a short video: motion, camera work, atmosphere and
  sound generated together, one to fifteen seconds. Give it a starting image and it animates
  that exact scene, so a picture made earlier in the workflow can be brought to life. A static
  image, and a live spoken conversation, are different jobs.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (who-can-run-it.md). Compulsory on every node.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: generation is non-deterministic, two runs are meant to differ.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# Text-to-video, short and small — the cheapest honest render (video bills per second).
# Asserts the SHAPE: a hosted URL and a plausible duration, never anything about the scene.

testData:
  config:
    prompt: >-
      A paper boat drifting across a puddle in light rain, gentle ripples, soft ambient
      sound, slow push-in
    imageUrl: ""
    duration: 4
    aspectRatio: "16:9"
    resolution: 480p
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    videoUrl: "return output.videoUrl.startsWith('https://')"
    video: >-
      return output.video.url === output.videoUrl
        && output.video.duration > 0
    metadata: "return output.metadata.generatedAt > 0"
